structure.title: Preface
structure.summary: This document is a notice from Bajaj Finserv Limited regarding its 18th Annual General Meeting (AGM) scheduled for 25 July 2025, along with the Annual Report for FY2025. It includes the AGM notice and annual report, business responsibility and sustainability report, and details of the AGM's ordinary and special business: adoption of financial statements, declaration of dividend, re-appointment of a director, ratification of cost auditor remuneration, and appointment of a secretarial auditor. The text also mentions availability of documents on the company and registrar websites and arrangements for members without email IDs to access the notice and annual report via web-link and QR code.

structure.title: Bajaj Finserv Notice of 18th Annual General Meeting 2025
structure.summary: The document is a notice from Bajaj Finserv Limited regarding its 18th Annual General Meeting to be held on 25 July 2025 at Hotel Hyatt Regency, Pune. It includes the company's registered office details, contact information, and the meeting's ordinary business: adoption of standalone and consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2025 with Directors' and Auditors' Reports, declaration of a dividend of ₹1 per equity share of face value ₹1, and appointment of a director in place of Manish Kejriwal, who retires by rotation and seeks re-appointment.

structure.title: SPECIAL BUSINESS:
structure.summary: The text outlines two special business resolutions for Bajaj Finserv Ltd.'s annual general meeting. First, ratification of remuneration of ₹80,000 plus taxes and expenses for Cost Auditor Dhananjay V Joshi & Associates for FY2026, appointed by the Board on the Audit Committee's recommendation. Second, appointment of M/s Makarand M. Joshi & Co., Practicing Company Secretaries, as Secretarial Auditor for five consecutive years from FY2026 to FY2030, with fees and expenses as per the annexed statement, and authorization to the Board to implement the resolution. The document is signed by Company Secretary Uma Shende, dated 29 April 2025, Pune, and references the 18th Annual Report 2024-25.

structure.title: NOTES
structure.summary: The notes cover proxy and dividend details for the AGM, including eligibility, appointment limits, deposit deadlines, inspection rights, and dividend recommendation, record date, payment date, and electronic payment mandate. SEBI KYC compliance requires physical shareholders to register PAN, KYC, email, and nomination via forms, and demat holders to update with DPs. Document inspection details are provided. Unclaimed FY2018 dividends and shares will transfer to IEPF in September 2025. Instructions for members/proxies cover attendance slip, ID, quorum, route map, joint holders, identity verification, and e-voting credentials. General information includes special business facts, institutional shareholder authorization, director appointment details, electronic distribution, e-voting grievance contact, scrutiniser appointment and report, and result publication. E-voting instructions cover eligibility, login methods, timelines, helpdesk, webcast, and dividend taxation.

nodes.title: Proxy and Dividend Information for AGM Notice
nodes.summary: The page provides proxy and dividend details for an AGM notice. Proxy rules cover member eligibility, proxy appointment limits (max 50 members/10% capital), deposit deadlines (48 hours before meeting), and proxy inspection rights (24 hours prior, with 3 days' notice). Dividend information includes a recommended ₹1 per equity share for FY2025, a record date of 27 June 2025, and payment by 29 July 2025. It mandates electronic dividend payment for physical shareholders lacking PAN, contact, bank, or signature details, effective 1 April 2024, and encourages updating bank details with DPs or KFin. Tax queries are referenced to note 30.

nodes.title: SEBI KYC compliance, document inspection, and IEPF share transfer notice
nodes.summary: The page outlines SEBI's mandate requiring physical shareholders to register PAN, KYC details, email, and nomination via forms ISR-1, SH-13, or ISR-3, with submission options and SEBI FAQs. Demat holders must update PAN, KYC, and nomination with their DPs. It details document inspection at registered and corporate offices from Monday to Saturday, 10:00 a.m. to 12:30 p.m., up to and at the AGM, covering the register of contracts, register of directors and KMP, and the secretarial auditor's ESOS certificate. Finally, it states that unclaimed FY2018 dividends will transfer to the IEPF in September 2025, with corresponding shares also transferred for seven-year unpaid dividends, urging members to claim.

nodes.title: Instructions for members/proxies:
nodes.summary: The notice outlines instructions for members and proxies attending the AGM: proxies must bring a filled attendance slip and ID, while members need a filled slip or QR code copy. In-person attendance counts for quorum under section 103. A route map is provided in the notice and on the company website. For joint holders, only the first-named holder can vote. Identity/signatures are verified via NSDL/CDSL for demat shares and KFin/company records for physical shares, and members should keep them updated. Members joining after notice dispatch but before the e-voting cutoff (18 July 2025) can obtain e-voting credentials from KFin via email from their registered ID, or register/update their email with DPs if unregistered.

nodes.title: General Information:
nodes.summary: This text outlines AGM procedural details: material facts for special businesses; institutional shareholder authorization requirements for representatives and remote e-voting; annexed director appointment/re-appointment and secretarial auditor details per SEBI regulations; electronic distribution of AGM notice, annual report, and other documents with website availability; reference to shareholder information chapter; e-voting grievance contact; appointment of scrutiniser Sachin Bhagwat; scrutiniser's vote counting, report preparation, and result declaration process; and publication of results and scrutiniser's report on specified websites and communication to stock exchanges.

structure.title: Your Company’s vision is to be a diversified yet integrated financial services entity with a pan-India presence and offer lifecycle financial solutions for its various customers.

Ltd., Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd., Bajaj Finserv Direct Ltd., and Bajaj Housing Finance Ltd. It also notes functional areas like Group Risk, Assurance & Human Resource, Private Equity Investments & Group Strategy, Investments, CSR, Corporate Affairs, Legal and Taxation, Insurance and Special Projects, and includes a page reference to the 18th Annual Report 2024-25.

structure.title: Corporate Information

It details the composition of key committees: Audit Committee, Stakeholders Relationship Committee, Risk Management Committee, Nomination and Remuneration Committee, Strategic Investment Committee, and Corporate Social Responsibility Committee, each with chairpersons and members, noting changes effective March and April 2025.

structure.title: Bajaj Finserv Leadership and Corporate Information
structure.summary: The page lists Bajaj Finserv Limited's leadership team, including presidents and managing directors of various subsidiaries, along with their roles. It also provides corporate information such as the Chief Financial Officer, Company Secretary, statutory and secretarial auditors, cost auditors, bankers, registered and corporate office addresses, and registrar and share transfer agent details. Additionally, it mentions sections for corporate overview, statutory reports, and financial statements.

structure.title: Building Responsible Businesses: Whole Greater than Sum of Parts FY2025 – The Year in Review
structure.summary: This FY2025 annual report excerpt covers Bajaj Finserv's diversified financial services, highlighting record consolidated total income of ₹133,822 crore (up 21%) and all-time high profit after tax of ₹8,872 crore (up 9%). It describes Bajaj Finance as the largest NBFC focused on tech-led innovation, digitalisation, and analytics, and Bajaj Housing Finance as among the largest and fastest-growing home finance companies with a full mortgage product range. It also covers Bajaj Finserv Asset Management's goal to be a full-stack AMC with active and passive products across debt, equity, and hybrid, serving 675,000 investors under a behavioral finance-based philosophy. Key metrics include consolidated AUM of ₹416,661 crore (up 26%), profit after tax of ₹16,638 crore (up 15%), and 43.42 million new loans booked (up 20%).

structure.title: Bajaj Finserv Limited: Financial Services and Health Tech Overview
structure.summary: The page covers Bajaj Finserv Limited's diverse financial and health businesses. Financial & Life Protection includes Bajaj Allianz Life Insurance, a fast-growing private life insurer, and Bajaj Finserv Direct, a digital marketplace and technology services provider with 96 unique partners and over 3 million transacting customers. Property, Casualty and Health Protection features Bajaj Allianz General Insurance, a leading profitable insurer with strong underwriting and innovation, reporting 12% individual rated business premium growth, 29% renewals growth, and 61% increase in individual term assets under management. Digital Stockbroker covers Bajaj Financial Securities, an all-in-one digital platform for demat, broking, and margin trade financing with 40% customer franchise growth. Health Tech presents Bajaj Finserv Health, a digital healthcare platform offering preventive to prepaid packages, OPD care, and telemedicine, serving 130 million lives annually. Financial metrics include gross written premium, assets under management, solvency ratios, and results overview headings.

structure.title: Strong Track Record
structure.summary: The text outlines a diversified financial services group with 18 years of experience, serving individual, SME, and corporate customers across India. It covers lifecycle needs including asset acquisition, protection, family/health investment, retirement/income, wealth management, and general insurance. Products and solutions include loans, insurance, annuities, ULIPs, fixed deposits, mutual funds, stocks, and savings, with digital access to a health ecosystem. Listed entities include Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Housing Finance, and Bajaj Finserv. Platforms and subsidiaries include Bajaj Finserv Direct (digital marketplace), Bajaj Allianz Life Insurance, Bajaj Finserv Asset Management, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance, Bajaj Financial Securities (digital stockbroker), and Bajaj Finserv Health (health-tech platform).

structure.title: Bajaj Finserv’s Journey through Time
structure.summary: The text outlines Bajaj Finserv's corporate overview, including statutory reports and financial statements. It presents a timeline from 2001 to 2025, highlighting key milestones: incorporation of insurance JVs with Allianz SE in 2001, formation of Bajaj Finserv in 2007, launch of various businesses (Bajaj Health, Bajaj AMC, Bajaj Ventures, BFSD Marketplace), and acquisitions. It includes a market capitalization chart from 2007 to 2025. FY2025 achievements are detailed: signing agreements to acquire Allianz's 26% stake in insurance JVs for 100% ownership, Bajaj Housing Finance's IPO of ₹6,560 crore, Bajaj Finance's pivot to BFL 3.0 as a FinAI company, Bajaj Finserv Health's acquisition of Vidal Healthcare Services, and Bajaj Finserv Direct turning cash positive.

structure.title: Our Priorities
structure.summary: Bajaj Finserv aims to be a financial lifecycle partner for every Indian by anticipating customer needs and offering financial inclusion, home loans, savings, protection, health, payments, and investments. It expands channels for discovery and service, with apps enabling 24/7 DIY transactions and fraud awareness. Customer obsession drives fairness, transparency, and innovation. The company notes its market share: 2.75% retail credit, third in general insurance, sixth in life insurance, and second in housing finance, indicating growth opportunities. Key metrics include 26 million new-to-credit customers included by BFL in six years, 19.7+ million farmers insured by BAGIC, 35.2+ million group lives covered by BALIC in FY2025, 192+ million lives serviced by Bajaj Finserv Health under Ayushman Bharat, affordable home loans launched by Bajaj Housing Finance, and 3.72 million QR codes at merchant POS by Bajaj Finance.

structure.title: 02 Transformation through Technology
structure.summary: The text outlines Bajaj Finserv's priorities in technology transformation, focusing on AI and Gen AI to enhance customer experiences and business growth. It details Bajaj Finance's shift to BFL 3.0, a FinAI company integrating AI across processes for improved engagement, revenue, and efficiency. Specific AI applications include conversational AI for sales, explainable AI for risk, AI-driven engagement and training, and co-pilot/auto-pilot in operations. It highlights data-driven businesses and new-age technologies as enablers. Key metrics include 300+ Gen AI projects, 603 million website visits, 70.6 million app installs, 81.8% digital servicing, 38.7% service requests via app/web, and 7.7 million loan repayment receipts. Bajaj Finserv Health's app-first approach and AI-led abuse management are also mentioned.

structure.title: 03 Efficiency in Capital Utilisation
key_items: Capital Efficiency – Insurance Companies; Capital Efficiency – Bajaj Finance
structure.summary: The text outlines Bajaj Finserv Limited's corporate overview, statutory reports, and financial statements, focusing on capital efficiency. It details strategies like franchise expansion, technology use, and diversification to maintain a robust capital position. For general insurance (BAGIC), it presents the combined ratio (99.6% 5-year avg vs industry 117.5% and top 5 private 106.3%) and GWP to capital invested trends from FY20 to FY25. For life insurance (BALIC), it shows market share of new business value among top 5 private peers (3.4% in FY20 to 7.4% in FY22) and GWP to capital invested trends. For Bajaj Finance, it compares ROE and ROA against industry averages from FY18 to FY25. The text also mentions priorities and sources.

structure.title: 04 Right Culture through People
structure.summary: This text outlines Bajaj Finserv's 'Right Culture through People' priority, emphasizing attracting, nurturing, and retaining top talent guided by a Culture wheel of Mindsets and Behaviours. It details succession planning through a 'grow from within' framework, listing key initiatives: the Group Young Leaders Program for tier-1 B-school hires, the Group Finance Associate Program for fresh CAs, One Finserv Careers for talent mobility, the 30-Under-30 talent acceleration program with a three-year journey, and Leadership Development for accelerated transitions. It also notes a workforce of over 104,000 colleagues.

structure.title: 05 Sustainable Long‑ term Growth for Stakeholders
structure.summary: The text covers Bajaj Finserv Limited's corporate overview, statutory reports, and financial statements. It emphasizes commitment to sustainable long-term growth for shareholders and contributing to India's inclusive economy, maintaining high compliance and corporate governance standards. It highlights sharing best practices, knowledge, and leadership across companies. It includes a share price change chart comparing BFS and Nifty50 over ten years with CAGR figures. It presents market capitalization and number of shareholders over fifteen years with CAGR. It mentions a listing ceremony of Bajaj Housing Finance with identified executives. It also references 'Our Priorities' and page number 21.

Stakeholder Engagement; Human Capital Management; Information and Cyber Security; Governance; Empowering Society
structure.summary: The text outlines the company's ESG priorities: environmental preservation with renewable energy generation; customer centricity with high CSAT, NPS, and low grievance ratio; financial inclusion via microfinance branches and group loans to women, plus government insurance coverage; stakeholder engagement; human capital management with employee development; information and cyber security with zero data breaches; governance through a board-approved responsible business policy; and empowering society via CSR projects, beneficiaries, and spend. It includes specific metrics for each area and references the 18th Annual Report 2024-25.

structure.title: 07 Our Commitment to Society: Corporate Social Responsibility
structure.summary: Bajaj Finserv's Corporate Social Responsibility section details its CSR priorities: youth skilling and empowerment through Bajaj Beyond, Skillserv, and CPBFI; children's well-being covering health, education, protection, and disability inclusion; and impact assessment. It also covers responsible business practices, FY2025 highlights, macroeconomic overview, consumer finance and lending (BFL, BHFL, Bajaj Broking), insurance (BAGIC, BALIC), emerging businesses (BFSD, Health, AMC), renewable energy (138 windmills, 65.2 MW), ESG integration, human capital development via One Finserv, financial performance, internal controls, awards, and cautionary statements including corporate governance.

nodes.title: Bajaj Finserv CSR Priorities: Youth Skilling and Empowerment
key_items: Shaping Better Futures for Youth of Today and Tomorrow
Skillserv: Skilling and Employability to Empower Youth
nodes.summary: The page outlines Bajaj Finserv's CSR commitment to shaping better futures for youth through Bajaj Beyond, covering skilling, child education, health, protection, and disability inclusion, with FY2025 CSR spend of ₹335.73 crore across 265 projects. It details Skillserv, a flagship skilling and employability initiative targeting youth and women from disadvantaged backgrounds, with 46,807 students trained, and 177,349 beneficiaries through grant-making skilling programmes. The self-implemented Certificate Program in Banking, Finance and Insurance (CPBFI) is a 120-hour module expanded via Project Odiserv across 60 Odisha colleges, and recognized by NCVET as an awarding body. Skillserv also pilots niche BFSI modules and digital programmes. Grant-making partnerships deliver diverse training and skilling programmes across sectors and demographics.

nodes.title: Bajaj Finserv Skilling and Empowerment Initiatives
key_items: Skill Development for Persons with Disabilities
nodes.summary: The page outlines Bajaj Finserv Limited's CSR initiatives across five areas: sector-specific vocational training for marginalized youth; healthcare skilling for paramedics and technical staff in rural, urban, and tribal areas; skill development for persons with disabilities, including intellectual and developmental challenges; self-employment and entrepreneurship support for micro and nano-enterprises, plus social startup incubation; and women's empowerment through training in healthcare, retail, hospitality, artisanal crafts, and food processing to enable income generation and economic independence. It also includes corporate overview, statutory reports, and financial statements sections.

nodes.title: Well-being of Children: A Comprehensive Approach
key_items: Cleft Care; Type 1 Diabetes Care; Paediatric Heart Care; Cancer Care; Epilepsy Care; Healthcare Infrastructure
nodes.summary: The text covers a comprehensive approach to children's well-being, including health, education, protection, and inclusion for persons with disabilities, with beneficiary statistics for each area. It highlights the PanIIT project for rural youth skilling with job placements, and details child health initiatives focusing on cleft lip and palate, heart diseases, paediatric cancer, type 1 diabetes, and epilepsy, through treatment, surgery, early diagnostics, screening, and awareness. It also mentions healthcare infrastructure improvements with equipment and training, and specific programs like Maha Smiles for cleft care, a Centre of Excellence for Type 1 Diabetes, and support for paediatric heart, cancer, and epilepsy care.

nodes.title: Bajaj Finserv CSR Initiatives for Children's Health and Education
key_items: Sai Sanjeevani Hospitals: Healing Little Hearts
nodes.summary: The page outlines Bajaj Finserv's corporate social responsibility priorities, focusing on children's health and education. It details the Sai Sanjeevani Hospitals' free congenital heart disease treatment, including surgeries, awareness, skilling, and a new ICU/OT expansion, illustrated by a patient story. It also lists educational interventions: child education, digital/tech-based learning, foundational literacy and numeracy, mental health, early childhood education, comprehensive school programs, vocational education, scholarships, and health and well-being check-ups. These initiatives aim to improve academic performance, employability, and overall well-being, aligning with government programs.

nodes.title: Child Protection and Vocational Education Priorities
key_items: Lend A Hand India: Real-World Skills for School Students
nodes.summary: The page outlines the organization's priorities, beginning with Lend A Hand India, which upgrades vocational education in 30 Pune schools for 3,000 students through lab refurbishment, educator training, industry exposure, internships, and monitoring, aligned with NEP 2020. Child Protection covers vulnerable children facing trafficking, abuse, child labour, legal conflicts, and juvenile delinquency via strategic partnerships. Institutional Care supports shelter homes and child welfare institutions. Rescue and Rehabilitation focuses on railway platform rescues and family reunification. Adoption and Daycare Support provides safe spaces and early childhood care for construction workers' children. Community Protection Programmes integrate education and protection to empower vulnerable communities. Aftercare and Transition Support offers ongoing guidance during life transitions. Awareness and Sensitisation raises community awareness about child sexual abuse.

nodes.title: Bajaj Finserv CSR: Disability Inclusion and Impact Assessment
key_items: Rehabilitation and Comprehensive Care; Educational Inclusion; Medical Rehabilitation; Assistive Technology; Community-based Inclusion; Competitive Exam and Fellowships
Measuring the Impact of Our Actions
nodes.summary: The page outlines Bajaj Finserv's CSR initiatives for Persons with Disabilities (PwDs), covering inclusion into mainstream society, rehabilitation and comprehensive care, educational inclusion, medical rehabilitation, assistive technology, community-based inclusion, and support for competitive exams and fellowships. It details efforts such as early identification and intervention, therapies, parental counselling, special schools, vocational training, aids and prosthetics, technological advancements, community-level projects, and exam support. Additionally, it describes the company's commitment to measuring the impact of its CSR actions, including assessments of 26 projects in FY2025 to evaluate outcomes, challenges, and inform decision-making.

nodes.title: Taking the Responsible Road Ahead
nodes.summary: The text covers Bajaj Finserv's responsible business approach, including child and youth development and multi-pronged interventions in Pune. It highlights Bajaj Housing Finance's mortgage products, describes Bajaj Finserv as an unregistered core investment company (CIC) with investment regulations, its renewable energy investments (138 windmills, 65.2 MW), and its financial reporting compliance with Ind AS and Indian GAAP for insurance subsidiaries, along with performance details of subsidiaries.

nodes.title: BFS: Highlights for FY2025
nodes.summary: BFS signed SPAs to acquire Allianz SE's 26% stakes in BAGIC and BALIC, making Bajaj group's ownership 100%. BFL surpassed 100 million customers and ₹400,000 crore AUM, becoming India's largest NBFC by AUM and PAT. BHFL completed a ₹6,560 crore IPO. BAGIC remained the 3rd largest general insurer by gross direct premium. BALIC held 6th rank in individual rated new business premium among top 10 private players, with AUM crossing ₹120,000 crore. Bajaj Finserv Health acquired 100% of Vidal Healthcare Services for hospitalisation claims management. BFS AMC achieved ₹20,365 crore AUM in its first full year, the fastest in the industry. BFS reported all-time high consolidated revenue of ₹133,822 crore and profit of ₹8,872 crore.

nodes.title: Macroeconomic Overview
nodes.summary: The text provides a macroeconomic overview from Bajaj Finserv Limited's report, covering IMF global growth projections (2.8% in CY2025, 3.0% in CY2026) amid trade tensions and policy uncertainty, with easing global inflation. It highlights India's real GDP growth at 6.5% for FY2025 (per IMF and NSO estimates), real GVA growth at 6.4%, quarterly GDP/GVA trends, and sectoral GVA growth (primary 4.4%, secondary 5.8%, tertiary 7.3%), noting manufacturing as a disappointment. It details moderating WPI, CPI-IW, and CPI-AL inflation; current account deficit at $11.5 billion (1.1% of GDP) in Q3 FY2025; RBI's GDP and inflation projections, and a 25 bps repo rate cut to 6%. It concludes India's economy is strong but flags US tariff escalation as a key concern.

nodes.title: Overview of Consumer Finance and Lending
nodes.summary: The text covers India's consumer finance and lending landscape, highlighting the shift from traditional banks to NBFCs, fintechs, and digital platforms. It details NBFCs' role in credit growth, GDP contribution, and financial inclusion, especially in underserved areas, providing faster services and priority sector lending. An outlook emphasizes NBFCs as key to sustainable growth. Chart A illustrates India's digitisation, including Aadhaar, UPI, ONDC, and fintech market projections. Risks and concerns include higher risk weights (with RBI rollback effective April 2025), funding constraints for smaller NBFCs, shallow bond markets, cost pressures, and challenges in overseas borrowing.

nodes.title: Overview of the Insurance Sector
key_items: Non-life insurance penetration as a % of GDP Non-life insurance density (US$)
nodes.summary: The text provides an overview of the Indian insurance sector, covering its structure (60 insurers, tenth largest globally, low penetration), FY2025 regulatory changes (consolidation, governance, policyholder interests, principle-based approach, rural expansion) and their mixed impact (muted growth due to surrender value and accounting regulations). It discusses industry initiatives (Bima Sugam, Bima Vistar, Bima Vaahak), investment performance (strong H1, selloff in H2), general insurance challenges (lower vehicle sales, health volume, fire rates, nat cat losses), a positive outlook (growth drivers), and key risks (natural calamities, cyber, market, tech disruption, competition). Includes a chart on insurance penetration and density for India and other countries.

nodes.title: Consumer Finance and Lending
nodes.summary: The section covers Bajaj Finance Ltd. (BFL), a leading NBFC, detailing its customer-centric digital strategy, cross-selling approach, and diversified financial services. It presents BFL's FY2025 consolidated performance, including customer franchise growth to 101.82 million, new loans, app customers, AUM growth to ₹416,661 crore, NTI growth, pre-provisioning profit, PAT, RoA, ROE, capital adequacy, and operational reach. It also covers Bajaj Housing Finance Ltd. (BHFL), a housing finance subsidiary, describing its mortgage products, IPO, and credit ratings, along with BHFL's FY2025 performance highlights such as AUM growth to ₹114,684 crore, NTI, PAT, and capital adequacy. The financial statements of subsidiaries are included in the consolidated financial statements from the date on which control commences until the date on which control ceases. nodes.title: Valuation framework (BFL)
nodes.summary:
Valuation framework (BFL)
BFL has an internal fair value assessment team which assesses the fair values of assets qualifying for fair valuation.
BFL’s valuation framework includes: • Benchmarking prices against observable market prices or other independent sources; • Development and validation of fair valuation models using model logic, inputs, outputs and adjustments; • Use of fair values as determined by the derivative counter parties.
These valuation models are subject to a process of due diligence and validation before they become operational and are continuously calibrated. These models are reviewed and validated by various units of the BFL including risk, treasury and finance. BFL has an established procedure governing valuation which ensures fair values are in compliance with accounting standards.

It also covers derivative instruments: cross currency interest rate swaps as cash flow hedges (Level 2 discounted cash flow using forward rates from zero coupon yield curve) and currency forward contracts (Level 2 using USD INR forward curve from Bloomberg). For amortised cost instruments, fair value is computed using discounted cash flow models with latest yields. For cash, bank balances, receivables, payables, short-term loans/debts, borrowings, overdrafts, and other current liabilities, carrying value approximates fair value.

Investments in subsidiaries and joint ventures are at cost per Ind AS 27, with impairment assessment. Derecognition of financial assets occurs when rights expire or are transferred with risks/rewards or control, with gains/losses in profit or loss. Financial liabilities are classified at amortized cost or FVTPL, initially measured at fair value, subsequently at amortized cost using effective interest method, and derecognized when obligations are discharged, cancelled, or expired, with gains/losses recognized in profit or loss.

structure.title: A. Short-term employee benefits and defined contribution plan
structure.summary: The text outlines accounting policies for employee benefits and equity arrangements: short-term benefits like salaries, leave, and bonuses are recognized as liabilities and expenses; contributions to defined contribution plans (superannuation, provident fund, pension) are expensed with no further obligation. Defined benefit gratuity plans are measured using actuarial present value of obligations less plan assets, with remeasurements in OCI and deficits recognized as liabilities. Compensated absences are actuarially valued. Equity-settled employee stock options are fair-valued using Black-Scholes, with costs recognized over vesting periods. Treasury shares held by an employee benefit trust are recognized at cost and deducted from equity, with no gain or loss on transactions, and share exercises settled with treasury shares.

structure.title: Employee Benefit Accounting Policies: Gratuity, Compensated Absences, Stock Options
structure.summary: The page outlines accounting policies for employee benefits. It covers recognition of bonus liabilities and periodic contributions to superannuation, provident fund, and pension schemes with no further obligation. Defined benefit gratuity plans are detailed: liabilities are present value of obligations less plan assets, actuarially calculated using projected unit credit method with assumptions on discount rate, salary escalation, attrition, and mortality; remeasurements go to other comprehensive income; payments are made to LIC and BALIC, with deficits recognized as liabilities. Compensated absences are recognized as liabilities based on independent actuarial valuation using projected unit credit method. The employee stock option scheme is equity-settled, fair value assessed using Black-Scholes on grant date, expensed over vesting period, with subsidiary employee costs recovered; cumulative expense reflects best estimate of instruments expected to vest, and no expense is recognized for non-vesting grants.

structure.title: E. Treasury shares
structure.summary:
E. Treasury shares
The Company has created an employee benefit trust (EBT) for providing share-based payment to its employees. The Company uses EBT as a vehicle for distributing shares to employees under the Employee Stock Option Scheme. The Company treats EBT as its extension and shares held by EBT are treated as treasury shares.
Own equity instruments that are re-acquired (treasury shares) are recognised at cost and deducted from other equity. No gain/(loss) is recognised in the Statement of Profit and Loss on the purchase, sale, issue or cancellation of the Company’s own equity instruments. Any difference between the carrying amount and the consideration, if reissued or sold, is recognised in capital reserve. Share options exercised during the reporting period are settled with treasury shares.

A. Current tax
Current income tax assets and liabilities are measured at the amount expected to be recovered from or paid to the taxation authorities, in accordance with the Income Tax Act, 1961 and the Income Computation and Disclosure Standards prescribed therein. The tax rates and tax laws used to compute the amount are those that are enacted or substantively enacted, at the reporting date. The money contributed by the Company to the fund to finance the liabilities of the plan has to be invested.
